newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to buy four mln tonnes Russian oil.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to buy four mln tonnes Russian oil.

text.p: Ukraine intends to buy four million tonnes of Russian oil for farming needs in November and December, a senior aide to the deputy prime minister responsible for agriculture said on Friday.
"A government order is being drawn up to buy four million tonnes of oil from Russia," Dmytro Stetsenko said by telephone.
"This oil will be refined in Ukraine and payment will be made either in cash or farm products."
Stetsenko said the oil would help ease chronic shortages of fuel in the farming sector.
He said the shortages were hindering Ukraine's sugarbeet harvest, with long delays in digging beets out of the ground and transporting them to refineries.
Some farm work, including processing of sunflowers and rice, also peaked towards the end of the year in southern Ukraine.
Stetsenko said the government required up to two weeks to prepare and issue the order to purchase the oil.
Ukraine's domestic annual crude demand is 15-20 million tonnes. The former Soviet republic has six refineries, most operating well below capacity.
In the Soviet era, the refineries routinely processed up to 60 million tonnes of crude annually.
But last year they refined only 16.8 million tonnes as Russian crude supplies fell. --Rostislav Khotin, Kiev newsroom +380 44 229 2264
